Hi Alyssa / Jordan —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Attached is a first-draft mutual action plan (MAP) tailored for the 3-week POC you outlined. High-level asks to get the environment ready: 

1) API keys & org setup
   - We can provision scoped ephemeral API keys for the POC. Request: create a Helsys test org (or add our service account) so we can bind the keys to the right tenant.

2) IP allowlist
   - Please provide the outbound IP ranges for your firewall. I attached a CSV template (network-allowlist-template.csv) to make this quick.

3) VPC peering (optional but recommended)
   - If you prefer VPC peering, we’ll need the VPC ID and a 2-hour maintenance window to validate route tables and MTU.

Proposed timeline (subject to your availability):
- 2025-07-09: Helsys provides test org invite + IP ranges
- 2025-07-11: Redwood issues POC API keys and initial smoke test
- 2025-07-14: Optional VPC peering window (if agreed)
- 2025-07-15: POC-ready handoff and baseline perf run

Please review the attached MAP draft (Helsys-MAP-Draft-2025-07-06.pdf) and flag any compliance or procurement items that would change these dates. If security wants to run a quick checklist, happy to loop them in.

Attachments: Helsys-MAP-Draft-2025-07-06.pdf, network-allowlist-template.csv

Best,
Ben

Ben — quick internal coordination after Jordan’s note. Forwarding with inline comments.

> Jordan: "Can you confirm the expected CIDR you’d peer with and the peering handshake steps?"

Our recommended approach for a tight POC (minimal security friction):
- API keys: issue scoped, short-lived keys (TTL = 6 hours) tied to a service account created inside the Helsys test org. We can automate rotation; recommend 6-12 hour TTL for active test runs.
- Org setup: request Helsys create a test org and invite redwood-poc@helsys.co (we’ll use a single service account). That lets us scope logs and audit events to the POC tenant.
- IP ranges: we’ll provide two outbound CIDR blocks (east/west) and a fallback range for bursting. I’ll have infra generate those by EOD today.
- VPC peering: to reduce risk, propose establishing a single peered subnet (/28) with strict route tables and only the ports needed for model payloads (443 + ephemeral control ports). Neha — can your infra team draft the peering playbook and the exact route-table change steps? Aim to share by 2025-07-09.

I’ll draft a short security checklist we can share with Helsys security to expedite approval.

—Rachel
